objective: Take up PROCESS-CONTACT-20261108-001's selected next step (G5, question 4, toward the program's first emergence): a contact that is a cell of two rings, so that both rings read it, binds both rings at every lag in only 44 of 128,128 configurations when it combines the rings' proposals, and at lag 1 it fails exactly when its own past fixes a proposal. Test whether a shared contact that does not read itself, combining its four ring neighbours (a parity of one function of each ring's pair), persists more often on the same rings; prove the lag-1 criteria of both contact families and the linear case; and measure how persistence changes as the rings grow, exactly at every lag where the dynamics repeats within a declared cap.
status: Complete 2026-11-08: at lag 1 a shared contact that combines the rings' proposals binds both rings exactly when its combiner is a parity and neither rule is canalizing at its centre, and a self-blind contact exactly when its table has no constant row or column; self-blind parities persist in 6.4% of configurations against 4.5% (H1 fails) but on 157 rule-size pairs against 22; persistence grows with ring size, from 1.1% to 20.5% (proposals) and 3.6% to 26.0% (self-blind) between 3 + 4 and 8 + 9 cells, so the rarity found by PROCESS-CONTACT was largely a small-ring effect. A31 confirmed. Next: two contacts across time (G5, with G1). Stress test at 9 + 10 running as SHARED-CONTACT-S1.
stop_rule: Stop when the lag-1 criteria are proved for both contact families, the census of contacts that do not read themselves is done on the declared rings and compared with PROCESS-CONTACT's, and the size trend is measured to the declared sizes, or an obstruction is found and explained.
title: Which shared contacts persist: a fifth to a quarter on larger rings
